query: What is Otto's position on scanning prints for critique, and what in Callum's message shows Callum already knew this before Otto had spoken in that thread?
gold: Otto opposes scanning, viewing it as a compromise that degrades the tonal range of a wet print — he said 'the print is the work' and that tonal range 'does not survive digitisation cleanly.' Callum revealed he knew this beforehand when he said 'Otto will have thoughts on the scanning part I imagine' — presenting Otto's likely objection as a predictable, known position before Otto had weighed in. The emoji and 'I imagine' signal that Callum is anticipating a familiar reaction, not speculating. He had prior knowledge of Otto's stance from earlier sessions or conversations and was flagging it as a known dynamic.
context:
[1] (about=Otto, episodic, t2 @2025-02-08T10:18:00) I will say what needs saying. Scanning is a compromise. The tonal range in a wet print does not survive digitisation cleanly. In my experience, the print is the work. I would rather members attended. That said, I understand the practical argument.
[2] (about=Callum, episodic, t2 @2025-02-08T10:13:00) makes sense to me. Otto will have thoughts on the scanning part I imagine 😄 lmk if we're putting it to a vote
[3] (about=Nora, episodic, t2 @2025-02-08T10:11:00) Also want to raise something before we start: we had two members miss sessions last month with no way to follow the critiques. Looking at a scan-sharing trial, where anyone who prints also produces a scan at 2400 dpi minimum. Thoughts? 🙂
[4] (about=Nora, episodic, t2 @2025-02-08T10:27:00) Decision: we will trial it for one month. Anyone who prints also produces a scan at 2400 dpi minimum. Happy to help with the process. 🙂
[5] (about=Otto, episodic, t10 @2025-03-08T10:07:00) I will send the contacts. Not the prints. In my experience the print is what matters, but I understand the practicality. The tonal range will read differently on screen.
[6] (about=Otto, episodic, t10 @2025-03-08T10:25:00) The thing people miss about digital scanning of silver gelatin prints is the compression of tonal range in the midtones. The shadows flatten first. Worth keeping in mind when reading scans critically.
[7] (about=Margot, episodic, t10 @2025-03-08T10:09:00) Nora explained the situation. Two members unable to attend. Scanning as the only way to include them in the critique. I suppose that is different from scanning as a general practice. It serves a purpose here.
[8] (about=Bex, episodic, t2 @2025-02-08T10:22:00) okay but Margot 'I see' could mean anything 😂 are you against it or just... thinking?? also I fully support the scan-sharing, it feels like it would make the group more connected between sessions 🙏
[9] (about=Nora, episodic, t9 @2025-03-08T10:03:00) Morning. Practical note: two members were not at the last session. As we agreed, scanning is the only way to include them in the critique. If you printed last week, please send a scan to the shared folder by Wednesday. 2400 dpi minimum. 🗓️
[10] (about=Priya, episodic, t10 @2025-03-08T10:21:00) From a compositional standpoint, the scan resolution does affect readability of fine detail. Worth agreeing a minimum standard per print type rather than a single number.
[11] (about=Otto, core, t2 @2025-02-08T10:05:00) Scanning is a compromise, the print is the work, prefers members attend, but understands the practical argument.
[12] (about=Otto, core, t14 @2025-03-22T10:07:00) Consistent paper type and tonal range across the show matters more than individual selection, variation in print quality is often missed.
[13] (about=Callum, core, t14 @2025-03-22T10:07:00) Large prints at the digital lab cost about twelve pounds per A2, better than using the collective budget.
[14] (about=Callum, core, t10 @2025-03-08T10:05:00) Provided scanning settings: 16-bit greyscale, Adobe RGB if colour profile needed, 2400 dpi minimum, offering a walkthrough.
agent_answer:
Otto’s position on scanning prints for critique is that scanning is a compromise: the tonal range of a wet print doesn’t survive digitisation cleanly, the print itself is the work, and he would rather members attend in person — though he understands the practical argument for scanning.

Callum’s message that shows he already knew this before Otto spoke is:  
**“Otto will have thoughts on the scanning part I imagine 😄”**  
Callum sent this at 10:13, before Otto’s own message at 10:18, showing Callum anticipated Otto’s reservations about scanning without needing to hear them first.
